thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: continuous-batcher latency > 2000ms (p95) in prod-us-east-1; error-rate rising; suspected KV cache churn.
ops-bot: Pager dispatched to on-call: Jamie (oncall) :bell:
Jamie (oncall): on it. looking at dashboards now — thanks.
Marisa: seeing queue depth jump across ~10 hosts, microbatch sizes collapsed to 1 in some shards? weird.
Sanjay: KV cache eviction rate spiked at 11:07 UTC, lots of small keys being churned. correlates with sudden ramp from client-app.
Jamie (oncall): any customer-facing errors?
Leo: 3 customers seeing high tail latency on generation calls, small percentage 0.6% but several requests timed out. I'll flag CS to triage.
Marisa: graphs: batch_wait_time increased -> workers filling, then microbatch sizes drop -> throughput cliff. Looks like jitter + very high concurrency.
Jamie (oncall): hypothesis: request arrival pattern produced microbursts that exhausted KV cache hotset causing eviction storms, KV misses forced recompute -> longer tokens -> increased queueing -> smaller microbatches -> vicious cycle.
Sanjay: agreeing. Also noticed continuous-batcher jitter parameter was recently relaxed in canary rollout (config: `batch.window_ms = 18 -> 50`). rollback might help.
Jamie (oncall): can we roll back batching window to 18ms on prod-us-east-1 canary group? quick config change.
Marisa: +1. but also need to throttle incoming concurrency if possible to buy time.
Leo: adding rate-limit on the edge for top noisy client org (org-42) to 10 rps as temporary mitigation. CS notified.
ops-bot: Running patch: `POST /api/v1/runtime/configs/prod-us-east-1/batcher -d '{"batch.window_ms":18}'`
ops-bot: Patch applied to canary pool (6 hosts). Monitoring rollout.
Jamie (oncall): roll back looks green on canary: p95 down from 2.8s -> 420ms. propagating to remaining pools slowly.
Sanjay: while propagating, I'll apply an emergency kvcache-pressure throttle: set `kvcache.per_client_rate_limit=500` to slow down churning clients.
Marisa: command?
Sanjay: `kubectl exec -it kvcache-controller -- /bin/sh -c "apply-config --set per_client_rate=500"` (run on prod-cfg cluster).
ops-bot: kvcache throttle applied to all controller pods in prod-us-east-1.
Leo: edge rate-limit in place for org-42; CS confirmed reduced errors.
Jamie (oncall): good. timeline: 11:06 UTC first alerts, 11:09 canary patch, 11:13 throttle, 11:15 rollouts 60% hosts, 11:22 stabilization on most hosts.
Marisa: still seeing a handful of hosts with high eviction churn — probably warm-up artifacts. I'll kick those through controlled restart to clear cache shards.
Sanjay: planning restart set: `for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l app=kvcache -o name); do kubectl rollout restart $pod --namespace=prod; done` — we'll sequential restart with 30s gap.
Jamie (oncall): please coordinate with me before each set of 5 pods. don't restart too many at once.
Marisa: acknowledged. running first window now.
ops-bot: Incident note: ticket auto-created INC-2026-984; severity P2.
Jamie (oncall): customer impact: small subset of real-time generation customers saw high p95/5xx for ~15-20 minutes. Majority unaffected due to fallback routes.
Leo: CS message drafted: "We observed an elevated latency window in us-east-1 affecting a small percentage of real-time generation requests. Root cause: cache churn + batching config interaction. Mitigation applied, ongoing validation." Sending now.
Marisa: after restarts and rollbacks, eviction rate back to baseline, microbatch sizes climbing back to expected distribution, overall throughput normalizing.
Sanjay: follow-up action: revert canary config change from telemetry pipeline and add guardrail to prevent batch.window_ms > 40ms by default. Also add a kvcache backpressure threshold to trigger auto-throttling before eviction storms.
Jamie (oncall): open an ops task for the guardrail + add an eval to repro this burst pattern. Assigning to Marisa and Sanjay.
Marisa: will write a small load harness to simulate microburst sequences and validate batch/jitter interactions.
Leo: update: customer org-42 reporting recovery. CS closing their tickets after validation.
Jamie (oncall): final status: mitigation successful, gradual rollout complete, active monitoring for next 2 hours. Logging timeline and actions to INC-2026-984.
Marisa: leaving postmortem stub in #postmortems. will link when done.
Sanjay: thumbs for follow-ups: add config validation, kvcache thresholds, and traffic shaping playbook.
ops-bot: Note saved to incident INC-2026-984 by Jamie (oncall).
Jamie (oncall): thanks all. switching back to monitoring. :white_check_mark:
